title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples — Ops & Canonical Fixes
author: Priya Malhotra
body:
Overview

This document consolidates our Developer Experience (DevEx) guidance for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. It is intended for DevEx engineers, solutions engineers, and docs contributors to maintain a consistent, high-quality set of developer-facing assets for Redwood Inference.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-first-success for new developers integrating with Redwood APIs.
- Standardize examples and templates across SDKs (Python, Node, Go, Java).
- Maintain an actionable runbook for docs-site operations and content triage.
- Capture top support issues and canonical fixes to reduce repeated support tickets.

Audience

- SDK engineers (authoring and maintaining SDK libraries)
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers (creating quickstarts and examples)
- Docs maintainers and site reliability engineers (docs-site ops)
- Support engineers triaging recurring developer issues

Structure of this doc

1) SDK Guide Standards  
2) Quickstarts & Templates  
3) API Examples (canonical snippets)  
4) Docs-site Operating Procedures  
5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes  
6) Ownership & Contribution Process

---

1) SDK Guide Standards

Intro: SDK guides should be authoritative, runnable, and consistent across languages. Each SDK guide page must include the sections below. Use the SDK guide template (see Quickstarts & Templates section).

Required sections for every SDK guide page:

- Short summary (1-2 sentences) describing intent and supported use cases.
- Quickstart (3-5 minute path) with copy-paste commands.
- Auth & configuration: environment variables, key rotation hints, KMS integration note if applicable.
- Key API patterns: code examples for common flows (text generation, streaming, chat, embeddings, reranking).
- Error handling: common exceptions and recommended retry/backoff logic.
- Best practices: batching, caching, token accounting, and cost controls.
- Compatibility & versioning: minimum runtime versions and migration notes.
- Tests & CI: how to run smoke tests and example unit tests.

Formatting rules:

- Use short headings and copy-friendly code blocks.  
- Example code must be idiomatic and limited to 12-20 lines per snippet.  
- Provide both synchronous and streaming examples where applicable.  
- Include a "What to expect" section with latency and cost tradeoffs for the example (approx values).

2) Quickstarts & Templates

Quickstarts are the recommended 3-5 minute onboarding flows. Templates are reusable repo scaffolds. Maintain one canonical quickstart per major SDK and a language-agnostic API quickstart.

Canonical quickstarts to maintain (priority order):

- python-text-generation-quickstart (Python)  
- node-chat-quickstart (Node.js)  
- go-embeddings-quickstart  
- java-batch-inference-template  
- rest-api-minimal (curl + JSON)

Every quickstart must include:

- Prereqs (SDK version, Python/Node version, env vars)
- Install steps with pin to a tested SDK release (example: pip install redwood-inference==0.12.3)
- Minimal runnable example (copy/paste) that returns a valid response
- Smoke test commands (curl or CLI) and expected output snippet
- Troubleshooting short list (2-5 items)

Repository templates should include:

- README with short and full quickstart flows  
- CI job file (GitHub Actions) that runs a documented smoke test using CI secrets  
- Example request/response fixtures under /fixtures  
- LICENSE file and CONTRIBUTING guidelines

3) API Examples (canonical snippets)

Provide short, copy-ready snippets for: text generation, chat with system instructions, streaming responses, function/tool-calling example, embeddings (single + batched), and reranking. Keep one canonical example per pattern and link SDK-specific variants.

Example (Python - text generation):

```python
from redwood_inference import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-small-1', prompt='Summarize the following text: ...', max_tokens=128)
print(resp.text)
```

Example (curl - streaming):

curl -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","prompt":"Hello","stream":true}'

Streaming note: clients must handle chunked framing and reconnect with resume token in event of transient disconnects.

4) Docs-site Operating Procedures

Purpose: keep the public docs site and internal doc portal synchronized, testable, and deployable with minimal downtime.

Owner: DevEx docs team (oncall rotation).

Key operational runbook steps:

1. Deploy flow: PR -> CI -> staging deploy -> smoke tests -> promote to prod.  
2. Staging smoke tests: run quickstart smoke tests (Python, Node) and a link-checker.  
3. Rollback: revert PR and redeploy previous artifact; run smoke tests.  
4. Post-deploy checks: search indexing, sidebar navigation, versioned SDK links.  

CI checklist (pre-merge):

- Linting: markdownlint, spellcheck for codeblocks  
- Code snippets: executed against snippet-runner (fail builds for broken snippets)  
- Link check: no broken internal links  

Emergency steps (docs-site down or snippets failing):

- Page-level outage: revert last merge and notify #devex-alerts.  
- Global search/index failures: rebuild index and monitor 30m.  
- Snippet regression causing support escalation: add patch with \"hotfix/snippet:\" prefix and request expedited CI priority.

5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes

This section lists the highest-volume developer support tickets reported in the last 12 months with the canonical fix to include in docs. Update monthly.

Issue 1: Authentication errors (401) after API key rollover
- Symptoms: \"401 Unauthorized\" immediately after rotating keys in the console.  
- Root cause: client code caches credentials or CI secrets not updated.  
- Canonical fix: document explicit steps:  
  1) Rotate key in Console -> copy new key.  
  2) Update environment variables in dev machine/CI.  
  3) Restart long-lived processes (workers, containers) that may cache the old key.  
  4) Verify with curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health`

Issue 2: Streaming disconnections and partial responses
- Symptoms: stream cuts mid-token or client receives a truncated message.  
- Root cause: transient network issues or insufficient client-side buffer and reconnect handling.  
- Canonical fix: include reconnection strategy and resume token usage in streaming examples; recommend exponential backoff and idempotency keys for retryable actions.

Issue 3: Unexpected embedding vector dimension mismatch
- Symptoms: client tries to store embedding vectors with incorrect expected dimension.  
- Root cause: model choice changed (new model uses different embedding size) or code assumes fixed size.  
- Canonical fix: for every embedding example, include `model` metadata and explicit vector dimension check snippet:  
  ```python
  vec = client.embed(text)
  if len(vec) != EXPECTED_DIM:
      raise ValueError(f\"unexpected embedding dim {len(vec)} (expected {EXPECTED_DIM})\")
  ```

Issue 4: High token usage from naive prompt looping
- Symptoms: unexpectedly high costs on monthly bill.  
- Root cause: prompt construction causing repeated stop tokens or recursive generation.  
- Canonical fix: document token accounting, show how to use `max_tokens`, and provide a small helper to count tokens before sending (link to token-counter utility).

Canonical fixes table (summary)

| Issue | Symptoms | Quick fix | Long-term doc change |
|------|----------|-----------|---------------------|
| Auth 401 on rollover | 401 after key change | Restart services & update CI secrets | Add rotation checklist + CI snippet |
| Streaming disconnects | Truncated responses | Implement reconnect logic | Add streaming resume sample in all SDKs |
| Embedding dim mismatch | Storage errors | Validate vector length before persist | Annotate models catalog with embedding dims |
| High token usage | Surprising bill | Add max_tokens and sampling limits | Add token-accounting quickstart |

6) Ownership & Contribution Process

- Page owner: assign to individual (DevEx engineer) and team (DevEx) in page metadata.  
- Review cadence: major docs reviewed quarterly; quickstarts reviewed monthly or after SDK releases.  
- Contribution workflow: fork -> PR with `docs/` prefix -> add `snippet-test` label -> request review from one reviewer and one SDK owner.  
- Release notes: maintain a short changelog block at the top of quickstarts noting the tested SDK version and date.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets

- Smoke test curl (health):
  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health

- Example GitHub Actions step (snippet test):
  - name: Run docs snippet runner
    uses: redwood/snippet-runner@v2
    with:
      token: ${{ secrets.DOCS_SNIPPET_TOKEN }}

- Token accounting helper (pseudo):
  def estimate_tokens(prompt):
      # refer to tokenizer table in models catalog
      return approx_len(prompt) * 1.1

Contact & escalation

- Primary team: DevEx (devex@redwood.ai)  
- Oncall: see rota in #devex-oncall  
- For product/security impacts: escalate to product-eng lead and security oncall
